1. Power On the Smart Car First, check if the battery voltage is between 11.6~12.6V—avoid overcharging or over-discharging. Then, insert the battery into the car and turn on the power switch. Finally, wait for the EdgeBoard to show a green light.
2. Connect to Computer 2.1 Wired Connection (First Connection) Use an Ethernet cable to connect the computer to the smart car Open the terminal and enter the command (may need multiple attempts if it fails): BASH Collapse Copy ssh edgeboard@paddlepi ssh edgeboard@paddlepi Enter the password: edgeboard to connect successfully. Note: If you cannot connect at this step, try multiple times. If it still doesn&rsquo;t work, contact me to replace the board.
2.2 Wireless Connection (Most Common) Wireless connection is commonly used when both the paddle and your computer are connected to the same hotspot. For the first wireless connection, enter the following in the terminal:
PLAINTEXT Collapse Copy sudo nmtui sudo nmtui Click &ldquo;active connect&rdquo; to connect to your hotspot. After that, to connect to the car, simply open your hotspot, wait for the car to connect, then enter in the terminal:
BASH Collapse Copy ssh edgeboard@paddlepi ssh edgeboard@paddlepi Password: edgeboard
3. Connect to VSCode via SSH 3.1 Install Plugin First, install Remote - SSH in VSCode—this is very easy.
3.2 Connect to EdgeBoard via Plugin Click the &ldquo;+&rdquo; button in ssh-remote Enter in the input field: PLAINTEXT Collapse Copy ssh edgeboard@paddlepi Password: edgeboard ssh edgeboard@paddlepi Password: edgeboard Click &ldquo;Allow&rdquo; all the way through. For the configuration file, select the first option (remember this configuration file location) Open the car-work folder in VSCode: PLAINTEXT Collapse Copy /home/edgeboard/car-work /home/edgeboard/car-work This step will fail 90% of the time. This document covers only the fundamental aspects of Git and Linux systems, which should be sufficient for most scenarios encountered in the Smart Car Competition. Beyond these basics, there are many advanced topics not covered here. Based on my experience, these advanced features are less frequently used in the competition, so I recommend learning them only when you encounter a specific need.
Furthermore, there is no need to study Git and Linux &ldquo;systematically&rdquo; from scratch; doing so will consume a significant amount of your time with minimal return for the competition itself. I encourage everyone to learn through practice and application rather than blindly pursuing theoretical mastery. Given my own limitations, please be understanding if there are any errors or inaccuracies in this guide!
1. Git Essentials 1.1 Why Use Git? Git is a widely-used distributed version control system, typically used in conjunction with GitHub or Gitee (Windows users can download it directly from the official Git website).
Remote Repositories: Create and manage codebases with GitHub/Gitee (Crucial). Version Control: Track and manage different versions of your code. Collaboration: Enable multiple team members to work on the same project. Using GitHub or Gitee to create a repository and regularly back up your code is vital! This prevents code loss in case the car&rsquo;s hardware fails unexpectedly. You should commit your code every time you finish a tuning session.
Recommended Workflow: Create local repositories on both the car&rsquo;s onboard computer and team members&rsquo; laptops, all linked to a single remote repository. Push code from the car and Pull code to the laptops to avoid merge conflicts.
1.2 GitHub or Gitee? Since our embedded boards (such as EdgeBoard or RK3588) usually connect via mobile hotspots, accessing GitHub directly can be unreliable without a proxy. For simplicity, I recommend using Gitee for code backups. The operations for Gitee and GitHub are …

1. Initialization 1.1 Installing Graphics Drivers BASH Collapse Copy sudo apt update ubuntu-drivers devices ubuntu sudo apt update ubuntu-drivers devices ubuntu 1.2 Locking Kernel Version Ubuntu enables the automatic kernel upgrade service by default when executing sudo apt update &amp;&amp; sudo apt upgrade. Kernel upgrades may cause unnecessary complications, so it is necessary to lock the kernel and then update the current software.
Check kernel version: uname -r Suppose it is 5.15.0-67-generic
Lock the current kernel version:
BASH Collapse Copy sudo apt-mark hold linux-image-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-headers-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-modules-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-modules-extra-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-image-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-headers-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-modules-5.15.0-67-generic sudo apt-mark hold linux-modules-extra-5.15.0-67-generic Verification: Enter apt-mark showhold to check if the lock was successful
Update software: sudo apt upgrade
